ios.desc:
Sift is a daily news briefing app that helps you understand world news — not just read headlines.
Instead of hundreds of updates, you get a focused daily news digest of the most important global stories — explained clearly, with context and meaning.

Understand the news, not just read it
Every story includes:
• why it matters to you
• what’s happening behind the scenes
• what could happen next

What you get every day
• a focused daily news briefing and summary
• important world news across geopolitics, business, technology, and science
• a daily insight to think differently — not just about the news
• no feed, no noise, no repeated stories

Built for clarity
No breaking alerts. No endless scrolling. No algorithm pushing outrage.
Just a clean, minimal news experience designed for focus.
If you want a news app that helps you understand the world without overwhelm, Sift is built for you.

Listen when reading isn't convenient
Prefer listening? Sift also offers audio news briefings, so you can stay informed while commuting, walking, or multitasking.

Terms of Use (EULA): https://sift-news.github.io/sift-data/terms.html

show_hn.title: Show HN: Sift – a minimal news app (looking for UI/UX feedback)

quotes.text:
I’ve been working on a small news app called Sift.

Looking for honest UI/UX feedback.

In screenshots the UI looks clean, but on real devices after installing it feels different — slightly dull / less crisp/ greyish. I can’t figure out if it’s colors, typography, spacing, or something else.

Would really appreciate direct feedback on:

what feels off or generic
anything that reduces the “premium” feel

Also not sure if this could be due to display differences or iPhone settings.

Blunt feedback is welcome.
